T01.title: HTTP client without traps
T01.desc: Implement WeatherClient(HttpClient) → GetAsync: request weather for the city via the implemented HttpClient. The behavior for each HTTP status, the number of attempts and the rules for releasing resources are specified below in the task conditions.
requirements: Perform a GET against BaseAddress: weather?city={Uri.EscapeDataString(city)}.
At 200, deserialize the JSON with the City and Celsius fields in Weather and return the result. Pass CancellationToken also when reading JSON.
For 404, return null immediately, without repetition. In this problem, null denotes no weather, rather than exhaustion of attempts or an arbitrary HTTP error.

Repeat only answers 429 and 5xx (500–599). Maximum of 3 HTTP requests in total: initial request and up to 2 retries. For example, 503 -> 503 -> 200 should be returned by Weather after the third request.
If all 3 attempts fail with a repeatable HTTP error, throw an HttpRequestException after the third response. There shouldn't be a fourth request. You cannot return null in this case.

For other unsuccessful HTTP statuses, including 400, 401 and 403, throw an HttpRequestException immediately, without repeating. For example, 400 → one request and an exception; 404 → one request and null.

In kata there are no delays between attempts. Replays of transport exceptions and JSON errors are not required: do not catch them to return null. Production Retry-After/backoff/jitter is explained separately.
Release every HttpResponseMessage via Dispose/using: on success, before retrying, on 404 and on exception. HttpClient belongs to the caller - don't close it.

Check the CancellationToken before the first HTTP call and pass it to SendAsync/GetAsync and read the JSON. The cancellation should propagate as an OperationCanceledException rather than being thrown into null or retry.
hints: Start with the API contract and response code table
Don't create a new HttpClient for every request
Don't use retry for an arbitrary non-idempotent operation
review: Typed results/errors
HttpResponseMessage.Dispose / using
No blind catch(Exception)
Tested with a dummy HttpMessageHandler
T01.answer: Typed client is registered via AddHttpClient<IWeatherClient,WeatherClient>. HttpClient is injected; response belongs to the call and is closed using. GET 404 -> null; 400 → error without repetitions. Only transient failures (in this specification 429 and 5xx) are repeated to a limited extent; take into account Retry-After, cancellation and the general deadline. Put Backoff+jitter into politics. OperationCanceledException do not absorb. Check sequences using fake HttpMessageHandler without a network. A lost response to a POST does not mean that the side effect did not occur.
T01.origin: A training exercise to prepare for technical interviews.

C46.title: EF Core: Atomicity of ExecuteUpdate and tracked audit
C46.desc: Implement Kata.TransferAsync(TxDb db,int fromId,int toId,int amount,Func<Task> afterDebit,CancellationToken ct). Affected rows and cancellation
The exception applies

C47.title: Async TTL cache: coordinate refresh per key
C47.desc: Implement AsyncRateCache without external packages. Cache exchange rates, not converted amounts. Concurrent requests for the same normalized currency coordinate a successful refresh; independent keys load in parallel.
requirements: Constructor: null load/clock throws ArgumentNullException; ttl<=0 or waitTimeout<0 throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. TimeProvider controls TTL only. waitTimeout is real lock-wait time, not fake time or a loader timeout.

GetAsync: null currencyCode throws ArgumentNullException; after Trim require exactly three ASCII letters, otherwise ArgumentException. Normalize with ToUpperInvariant before cache lookup, coordination and load. Pass the normalized key to load.
An entry is fresh only while clock.GetUtcNow() < storedAt+ttl. Equality means expired. TTL starts after a successful load completes. Fresh hits bypass lock waiting.

At most one load at a time per normalized key in this cache instance. Recheck freshness after waiting. Different keys must not block each other. Any implementation with this observable behavior is accepted.

Failure to acquire within waitTimeout throws TimeoutException. Zero timeout is allowed and fails immediately for an occupied key. Never release an unacquired permit. The timeout does not bound load execution.

After validation check ct before reading/working, pass it to waiting and load, and check cancellation after load before publishing. Canceling a waiter must not cancel another caller’s load. Owner errors/cancellation propagate and release coordination.
Do not cache null, exceptions or canceled loads. Later callers may retry; failure coalescing and stale fallback are not required. Do not return expired values on provider failure.

Keep signatures. Cleanup of per-key coordination is not required for the bounded three-letter key space. Eviction, distributed locks, jitter and retries are discussion topics, not hidden grading requirements.
cases: Fresh hit and exact TTL boundary
hints: Separate container safety from the invariant of the entire load operation.
Recheck state after waiting: another caller may have populated the cache.
Only an acquired permit has an owner. Null and exceptions leave no fresh value.
review: Normalize before coordination
Recheck after waiting
Release only acquired permits
Avoid global serialization
Explicit error and cancellation policy
C47.answer: One option uses ConcurrentDictionary entries and per-normalized-key SemaphoreSlim gates. Check a fresh hit first; await WaitAsync(waitTimeout,ct), throwing TimeoutException on false before entering the owner try/finally. Recheck freshness, invoke load with ct, check cancellation and publish non-null data with its completion timestamp. Release in finally. Use the gate returned by GetOrAdd; its factory may run more than once. Removing a gate after Release is unsafe while other callers retain it. This contract does not promise a single provider call across failures or coordinate multiple processes.
